Charred stone and melted glass for a hundred metres in every direction. Whatever happened here was catastrophic.
A torn page from a research journal: \'The convergence experiment exceeds all projections. We must press on.\'
Arcane matrices etched into the surviving wall sections — a containment circle, poorly designed, clearly overstressed.
A passage has been blasted open downward. Constructs still move in the dark below, following old instructions.
The passage descends into intact chambers beneath the rubble. The Arcane Ruins still function, after a fashion.
The water here has no bottom. Strange lights pulse from impossible depths.
Fish pulled from the deep glow faintly and dissolve within minutes. What fed on them?
A torn map marks this lagoon with a single word: \'DO NOT FISH.\' No explanation is given.
Something rises to the surface and sinks again. Massive. Ancient. Curious.
The dark water parts. The Abyssal Ruins loom below — vast, alien, and ancient beyond reckoning.
Strange stone pillars rise from the grotto floor, carved with script no living scholar can read.
The fish scatter without warning — something large passes below.
A waterlogged journal drifts by: \'The temple they found beneath the water was not abandoned. It was waiting.\'
A submerged archway pulses with faint ancient light. The current pulls toward it.
The archway is clear. The Drowned Temple lies beyond — something old watches from within.
Ancient rune-carved walls pulse faintly. The dwarves who built this place are long gone.
A colossal forge stands at the passage end, its fires somehow still burning after centuries.
Iron golems stand dormant in the alcoves. Their eyes flicker as you mine nearby.
The forge runes are a warning — something was bound here, and it grows restless.
The golems rise fully to life. The Ancient Forge awakens — its guardians await those brave enough to enter.
The trees here bleed shadow where cut. The wood writhes and resists the blade.
A shadow beast watches from the canopy. It does not attack — it only observes.
Old sanctum stones are visible through the twisted trunks. Something still lives there.
The corruption spreads as you work. The canopy hungers for something unnamed.
The canopy parts. The Corrupted Sanctum rises from the shadow-wood — its doors open, waiting.
The trees here whisper in a language older than any known tongue.
Stone foundations visible beneath the roots — the remains of something built long before the forest.
A druid\'s warning carved in bark: \'The clearing at the grove\'s heart is not what it was. Stay away.\'
Corrupted vines reach toward you as you chop. The grove resists your presence.
A gap in the canopy reveals ruins at the grove\'s heart. The Ancient Forest Ruins call to be explored.
A crumpled ledger page: names, dates, and numbers. Someone has been tracking payments to a person called the Warden.
Scratched into the wall: \'For those who prove themselves — the Sanctum awaits. Ask no questions.\'
A torn letter warning a member to stay away from the eastern tunnels. No reason is given.
A wax-sealed map fragment. The seal is unfamiliar — a shadow behind a locked door.
The last passage opens into a vaulted chamber. At the far end, a reinforced door bears the same seal. The Rogue Sanctum lies beyond.
Fresh rope marks on the windowsills. Someone uses this tower regularly.
A hidden cache inside a cracked wall: lockpicks, a short blade, and a coded ledger.
The ledger is a tally of stolen goods and split payments. The rogues operate out of somewhere beneath the hill.
A trapdoor in the floor, recently oiled, its hinges silent. Worn boot prints surround it.
The trapdoor opens onto a carved stairway going deep into the earth. The Shadow Den waits below.
Scratches mark the tunnel walls, too deep and wide for any pickaxe.
Old mining equipment, twisted and bent. Whatever was here left in a hurry.
A miner\'s torn note: \'We broke through to something below. The foreman sealed the lower shaft. He won\'t say why.\'
Tremors from below. Dust falls from the ceiling in slow waves. Something stirs.
The sealed shaft gives way. A vast cavern opens beneath — the Collapsed Mine lies ahead.
A dossier on every major merchant in the city. Someone has been compiling this for years.
A vault door, partially ajar. Inside — crates of stolen weapons, armour, and sealed scroll cases.
One scroll case is different from the others. It bears the seal of the royal treasury. It is empty.
A private journal: \'The Guild of Shadows is not just a guild. It is a government. They have always been watching.\'
The deepest vault is not locked. It is guarded. What waits inside is the Guild\'s greatest secret — and its most dangerous protectors.
